slides.0.title: The Aconcagua zone: Aconcagua Valley, Casablanca and San Antonio
slides.0.subtitle: From a warm valley sheltered by mountains to a cool coast shaped by the cold current
slides.1.title: Three sub-regions of the Aconcagua zone
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Three sub-regions
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth splits the Aconcagua zone into Aconcagua Valley, Casablanca Valley and San Antonio (including Leyda); Wikipedia lists Aconcagua Costa as well, so sources divide it slightly differently
slides.1.highlights.1.title: From warm to cool
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Aconcagua Valley is warm and known for Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah; Casablanca and San Antonio are cooled by the Pacific and excel with white grapes
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Location
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Aconcagua Valley lies about 65 km north of Santiago (Wikipedia); Casablanca is about 70 km west of Santiago (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: From inland to the sea, the zone runs from a warm red-wine valley to cool white-wine country.
slides.2.title: Aconcagua Valley: a warm pocket behind the mountains
slides.2.highlights.0.title: A mountain barrier
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Decanter describes a corridor of mountains that keeps out the ocean influence, making it one of Chile's warmest microclimates; large day-night swings strongly affect colour development
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Climate and soils
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia: a Mediterranean climate with about 215 mm of rain a year; soils are clay and sand in the east, granite and clay in the west
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Seña and the Berlin tasting
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Seña is Errázuriz's joint venture with Mondavi; at a blind tasting in Berlin in 2004 it placed ahead of Château Lafite and Château Margaux (Wikipedia)
slides.2.content: Aconcagua Valley is a warm pocket made by a mountain barrier and an important source of Chilean reds.
slides.3.title: Casablanca Valley: Chile's cool-climate pioneer
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Fog and sea breeze
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Morning fog from the cold Humboldt Current drifts inland and afternoon breezes arrive from the west; about 25 km from the Pacific, at 200–400 m (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Sauvignon Blanc is the leading variety and Chardonnay the second; Pinot Noir and cool-climate Syrah are secondary (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Risk and beginnings
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The main risk is spring frost (September–November); the start is placed in the early to mid-1980s, and Wine With Seth records Pablo Morandé planting experimental Chardonnay at Tapihue in 1982
slides.3.content: Casablanca is the benchmark for Chile's cool-climate whites, and fog and sea breeze are its keywords.
slides.4.title: San Antonio and Leyda
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Closer to the sea
slides.4.highlights.0.content: San Antonio is shaped by the Pacific; Wine With Seth names Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay as its benchmarks, with Pinot Noir growing in importance
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Leyda
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Leyda is a zone within San Antonio; Decanter's Aconcagua feature mentions the producer Viña Leyda
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Data limits
slides.4.highlights.2.content: This lesson did not obtain altitude, rainfall or area figures for San Antonio and Leyda, so they are not tested
slides.4.content: The closer to the Pacific, the cooler it gets, which is why whites and Pinot Noir are prized here.
Which three sub-regions does Wine With Seth give for the Aconcagua zone?
A. Aconcagua Valley, Casablanca Valley, San Antonio (including Leyda)
Leyda is a zone within San Antonio.
Where does Casablanca's morning fog come from?
The cold current brings morning fog, followed by afternoon sea breezes.
Sauvignon Blanc leads, with Chardonnay second.
Wine With Seth names spring frost as the main risk.
Aconcagua Valley is warmer than the coastal sub-regions mainly because?
A. A mountain corridor blocks the ocean influence
B. It is at a higher latitude
C. It sits on a volcano
D. It has no day-night swing
Seña is a joint venture between which two parties?
B. Concha y Toro and Mouton Rothschild
Both Decanter and Wikipedia say so.
